svg.title: FIG-25 Copied UART TX: current software ownership Actual kernel entry / NS RTOS / HIL and full IO-39/SOC-36 exits remain open
svg.desc: Untrusted caller Scalar device / session / slot / epoch Transient TX bytes and reply span; Kernel-invoked dispatch Trusted principal before copies Fault-contained snapshot; no retained user address; Exact privileged copied cells Request + copied TX bytes No second FIFO or worker; One existing BusOwner FIFO UARTOwner + selected UART port External executor advances real hardware; Required final-access predicate Acquire Core SETTLED + owner idle Actual UART/IRQ and publisher withdrawal; Retire copied result cells CONSUME: successful reply copy OR closed REAP: trusted drained proof Then detach + wipe; preserve epochs; Final JOIN Closed + all cells retired + owner idle Authority release SUCCESS permits reclaim; Trusted kernel/session authority Unique actual-owner role + persistent history identity / claim / drained / release; Trusted serialized kernel owner Explicit service / cancel / close / reap / join No implicit scheduler or provider stop; Failure retains responsibility QUARANTINED keeps copied borrow Proof/release failure keeps role and storage; copied scalar protocol + transient bytes; each entry: identity construction only: exclusive session claim; SUBMIT: copy before admission; borrows request + privileged payload; calls existing service / cancel; real drain; final publication; publisher exits; terminal state alone does not free the cell; REAP only: old gateway observers joined future entry blocked; role stays claimed; closed trusted REAP; no user action; only after every copied cell retires; JOIN only: outer observer join + role release; failed actual drain / QUARANTINED; failed copy / proof: no wipe; failed release: no reclaim; external recovery + continued service while hardware still owns the request
